findings.title: Mount-failure teardown calls `destroy()` on a provider whose `create()` threw
findings.description: When `provider.create()` throws, the catch block calls `teardown()`, which calls `provider.destroy()`. The real `LightweightChartsProvider.destroy()` starts with `assertReady()` (`src/chart/providers/lightweight-charts-provider.ts:67-69`). That throws "not ready" if `chart` is still null. If `create()` failed inside `createChart`, `chart` is null. Teardown then logs a second, misleading `provider teardown failed` error that masks the real failure. The unit tests didn't catch this because the spy's `destroy()` never throws. The test "tears down after a failed create" asserts `destroy` was called once, which is the behavior that triggers this on the real class. Track whether `create()` completed and skip `destroy()` if it didn't. Alternatively, make the failure path dispose only what was actually built. A test against the real provider, or a spy whose `destroy` throws when it wasn't created, would cover this.

findings.title: `error` keeps the latest failure, but docs and a test name say "first"
findings.description: `UseChartProviderResult.error` is documented as "The first error from any provider operation" (`src/chart/chart-operations.ts:77`). The test is named "keeps the first error rather than being reset by a later success". `setOperationError` does `setMount((current) => ({ ...current, error: failure }))`, so a second failure overwrites the first. The test only checks that a later success doesn't clear the error. It never checks that a second failure leaves the first one in place. Either preserve the first error (`current.error ?? failure`) or change the docs and test name to "most recent". Also add a test with two failures.

findings.title: Theme-token lookup silently falls back to library defaults
findings.description: `readChartStyle()` returns `undefined`, or leaves individual fields `undefined`, when a CSS token resolves empty. The provider then uses the library's white default, so a renamed or missing token gives a white chart with no error. CLAUDE.md says "Never use silent fallback values. Fail explicitly." The e2e test would catch a total failure, but a single missing token such as `--color-grid` would pass unnoticed. Throw (or surface through the hook's `error`) when a required token is empty.

findings.title: Mount-time subscriptions use no-op handlers (dead code)
findings.description: Both `subscribeCrosshairMove` and `subscribeVisibleRangeChange` are registered with callbacks whose only body is `if (disposedRef.current) return`. The indicator effect (`:348-358`) likewise has an empty body. This adds subscriptions and effect runs that do nothing, plus about 40 lines of explanatory comment. It also adds failure paths: a subscribe throw now fails the whole mount. The justification is "proves the disposer lifecycle", which the tests could do through the facade. The CLAUDE.md "resist complexity" principle argues for removing these until initiative 120 needs them. If they stay, they should at least be called out as intentional scaffolding in the slice docs.

findings.title: Hook file exceeds the ~300-line guide, and its lint suppression is file-wide
findings.description: The file is 366 lines and the mount effect is about 150 lines, against the ~50-line function guideline. The `eslint.config.js` comment justifies disabling `react-hooks/refs` for the whole file partly by saying inlining the facade would keep the file about 60% over the guide. It is still over. The file-wide `off` also hides any real ref-during-render mistakes later added to this file. Consider extracting the mount sequence (create, resize, observer, subscriptions, teardown) into a plain helper that returns a disposer. That would shrink the effect and might let the rule stay enabled. If the suppression stays, use a targeted `eslint-disable-next-line` at the `useMemo` call instead.

findings.title: Range translation is skipped when the first series is added after the range was set
findings.description: The range effect checks `seriesCountRef.current === 0`, but the ref is not state, so adding the first series does not re-run the effect. If the range was set while the chart was empty, adding a series does not apply that range. The next `range` change does. The comments describe this as a seam for initiative 120, but the behavior is a latent bug: the viewport stays out of sync with Context until the user changes the range. The test only covers "add series, then change range". Track the series count as state, or have `addSeries` re-apply the current range. At minimum, document and test the "range already set before first series" case.

findings.title: Inconsistent import extensions in routes
findings.description: `router.ts` imports `./routes` and `./chart-route` without extensions. The new hook, test, and App files use explicit `.ts`/`.tsx` extensions. This is minor, but the repo now has two import styles side by side.

findings.title: Test hygiene
findings.description: `LINE_SERIES` is declared between import statements, so later imports follow executable code. The tests also lean on several `as` casts (`as DOMRect`, `as unknown as`) and on non-null assertions (`box!`, `seriesId!`) with no explanatory comments. The test files live under `src/test/` rather than a package-level `tests/` directory. This may be an existing project convention, so I'm not flagging it as a violation. Another gap is that the e2e `smoke.spec.ts` comment refers to `chart-render.spec.ts` for the chart assertions, but the new live-chart assertions are in `chart-live.spec.ts`.

findings.title: Harness gating and Context/facade design
findings.description: The mode gate uses direct `===` comparisons so Vite can fold it statically, and `playwright.config.ts` builds in `e2e` mode to match. The forwarding facade routes every operation through one guarded runner and does not expose `create` or `destroy`. The disposer registration avoids the `push(a(), b())` leak, and the teardown order is sound. The facade has stable identity and tests that check it. The `ChartOperations` types are explicit, with no `any`.
